blocks.text: Last year I ran the city 10k in 56:40. I went out too fast and walked twice after the 7 km mark. This year I want to finish under 50 minutes.
The plan is to run four days a week and hold 5:30 per km on every run, so my legs learn race pace. If I hold 4:55 for the whole race, I’ll come in just under 50.
Sunday is the long run. I’ll add a kilometre every week until I reach 16.
Strength work twice a week, mostly calves and hips, because that’s where it fell apart last year.

threads.quote: If I hold 4:55 for the whole race, I’ll come in just under 50.
threads.first_quote: If I hold 5:30 for the whole race, I’ll come in just under 50.

messages.text: At 5:30 a km, 10 km takes 55:00. Under 50 needs 5:00 a km or faster; 4:55 leaves a little room. Which do you want to change: the pace or the goal?
4:55 a km comes to 49:10. That works.

threads.quote: add a kilometre every week until I reach 16

messages.text: Starting from how far? If you start at 8 km, 16 km is eight weeks out. Is the race at least eight weeks away, with an easier week before it?
You walked after 7 km last year. Is pace the problem, or the last 3 km?
Then the long run matters more than the pace work. Which of the four days is the long one?
Then Sunday decides the race. What does a Sunday look like in week six?
What should the strength work be?
What gave out first last year, your calves or your form? Start from that and the exercises pick themselves.
